changes: First build researched for this wiki (the research notes on the [Mechanics reference](/mechanics-reference) quote this build).

Every weapon, passive, item, enemy, boss, biome, event, dog and recipe is identical, as are the difficulty table, wave table and UI text. The only gameplay change: a drop that would land on an unused point of interest is moved off it, staying on screen if it dropped on screen (`pickups.movedDropInView` 120).

Content, English text, game config values, difficulty table and icons are identical. Removed: the drop relocation rule from the previous build; the step that nudged points of interest apart when the world is generated; and the step that moved a Root Tunnel exit off other points of interest. Added: when a Spud Freezer only catches bosses, its message says how many bosses were slowed; shared run pages show the difficulty level; a new whirlpool look for the Stand Mixer.

Content, English text, game logic, difficulty table and icons are identical. Added: a link such as `https://tibo.dog/?difficulty=hard` starts a run on that level straight from the title screen; Auto quality can now step back up when the game runs smoothly (Apple GPUs on touch devices start on Medium); weapons got element-coloured hit sparks; analytics waits up to 20 s instead of 3 s to learn the player's region before asking for consent.
Content, English text, game logic, difficulty table and icons are identical. The only change: while the screen is fully dark during story mode's knock-down sequence, the on-screen banners are hidden.

Content, English text, game logic, difficulty table and icons are identical. The only change: the renderer no longer prepares the intro cutscene when the intro will be skipped (a `?difficulty=` link or skip-intro start), which shortens loading.

Touch dash flicks are detected differently: a stroke of at least 30 px over the last 120 ms, moving at least 400 px/s on release or 900 px/s while held (was 22 px within 260 ms). Adds a season schedule to the config. Game data and difficulty are unchanged.

Normal is no longer the plain defaults: fewer pests (×0.7), pest HP ×0.65, enemy damage ×0.55, boss and elite HP ×0.65, Tibo max HP ×1.5, XP ×1.3, 1 extra revive, enemy tiers lag 2 minutes and fewer wall pests (×0.3). POI charge sounds can overlap (up to 4 voices).
Game data, English text, difficulty table, icons and game logic are identical (renamed code only).
Adds a server clock check (`/api/time`). No gameplay changes.

Balance pass. Base weapons hit harder at several levels (Deep Fryer, Hash Brown Shield, Julienne Dash, Mezzaluna, Potato Battery, Potato Rain, Root Cellar, Root Spikes) and Butter Streak cooldown drops from 3.5 s to 2.5 s. Every evolution gets more damage, most also shorter cooldowns or more projectiles; Spud Grid wires can now latch onto bosses (`clipsBosses`). Proc items are roughly doubled (Heavy Russet, Spicy Croquette, Static Tot, Wandering Eyes, Coal-Baked Spud, Porcupine Spud) and Boom Spud kill explosions rise from 8% to 12%. The Spud Freezer now freezes every enemy on the map for 7.5 s (was pests within 200 units for 5 s).
Analytics only. No gameplay changes.

Hard and Nightmare are much easier. Hard now nearly matches Normal (pests ×0.75, pest HP ×0.65, damage ×0.6, boss HP ×0.7, max HP ×1.5, XP ×1.3); Nightmare drops to pests ×1.05, pest HP ×1.2, damage ×0.95, boss HP ×0.95, elite HP ×1.3 and gains max HP ×1.2. Both now lag enemy tiers by 2 minutes and their opening crowds ramp up later. Dogs are Legendary twice as often (1/3, was 1/6). Adds a P key to pause.

The main game config, story script and a few tables moved from the sim chunk to the boot chunk; the wiki now finds them in either. Revives outside Story play the same knocked-down scene as Story, then Tibo gets up with 50% HP and 2 s of invulnerability; level-ups earned while down wait until then. Screen clears (`nuke` weapons such as Reset Button) now take only 5% from bosses (was 25%). Armor, dodge and crit item and passive descriptions no longer show point values. Game data otherwise unchanged.

Nightmare's late damage ramp now starts at 5:00 instead of 15:00, adding 0.064 per minute instead of 0.2. Snacks drop 20% less often on Nightmare (normal pests 0.32%, Crop Patches 28%); their healing is unchanged. Nightmare adds alternate bullet patterns for amusing, Colorado Queen, The Masher, Late Blight, Sir Strawman, The Fryer King, Blight Spore and Ice Imp. Vampire Tot heals 0.05 HP per kill (was 0.15); Hash Bulwark's guard burst rises from 72 to 86. Meteor Russet delays its triggering hit by 0.4 s; the area blast lands at the original trigger position (see its item page for target and capacity rules). Story's starting-kit offer now waits for the current line's reading time. Adds an Update game button on the title and pause screens when a newer build is available, with confirmation during a run; pause also shows the game commit. Refreshes meteor, projectile-trail, landmark, ground and evolution visuals. The difficulty table changes its internal balance targets to `mixReach`; these are not measured survival rates. Icons are unchanged.

Cursed extra bosses now use floor(curses taken × 0.25), down from ×0.5: the first extra boss needs four curses taken (four Moldy Shrines, or three on Nightmare with its starting curse). Nightmare no longer shows enemy shot-path markers; Easy, Normal and Hard keep them. Peel Forest props per chunk drop from 20 to 12, and frozen-crate sprites shrink to 85% scale. Missed amusing spawns are replayed when its entrance finishes loading, without repeating the spawn sound. Phone dialogue now replaces an older pending conversation instead of queuing it, removes typing delays, and shows Alex's join line after he joins. Improves sprite texture packing and updates the in-game changelog. Other content values, English content descriptions, difficulty multipliers, simulation logic and wiki icons are unchanged.

Outside Story, revives now grant 4 s of invulnerability (was 2), push nearby visible pests and bosses with strength 900 in a 160-unit radius plus their body radius (was pests only, strength 400 within 120), freeze pests and elites for 5 s, slow bosses to 50% speed for 5 s and delay their next pattern, and clear shots within 160 units. Story keeps its previous revive rules. Ice Imp's Nightmare fan bullet speed rises from 85 to 130. Enemy shots get animated orbs and shooter-specific shapes, including oil drops, grinder comets and maggots; Low quality omits shot smears. Main-thread effect loading now prioritizes important sheets and budgets work to the viewport and frame time. Game config, story configuration, Alex/phone controllers and live scoring move from boot to sim; scoring rules and other balance values are unchanged. Expands the in-game changelog, including notes for older releases. English content descriptions, difficulty multipliers and wiki icons are unchanged.

Nightmare adds larger ground attacks centred on Tibo's position: the Masher strikes a disk and two rings 0.35 s apart, Late Blight places a central pool plus six satellite pools, and the Fryer King strikes six wedges in alternating sets 0.5 s apart, leaving oil puddles after the second set. These layouts use distances ×1.45; ordinary attacks on other levels are unchanged. Outside Story, items and chests without a choice can show icon loot notices while the run continues; choice chests keep panels. Notices arriving within 1.5 s merge and last 3 s. Evolutions get icon banners too. The Harvester's shots now look like tumbling grain kernels, with flashing tied to the flashes setting. Improves ground-warning and ring rendering. One Story lasso line now suggests asking a Grok Bot for directions. Other balance values, English content descriptions and wiki icons are unchanged.

Tater Slots now adds gold to both winning outcomes: three of a kind gives a 1-reward chest plus four current spin prices of bonus gold; a pair gives a random item plus half a spin price, rounded to the nearest gold. The bonus is calculated at payout and is not multiplied by gold gain. Adds glints to held weapons, trails and launch flashes to on-hurt item shots, firing flashes/sparks/casings for Fry Sentry, Fry Brigade and Tater Pup, and sparkle/shatter effects for Hash Brown Shield and Hash Bulwark. Healing, pickup and reward rings use sharper pixel-sized bands. Shared-run pages withhold reconstructed scores for capped kill totals, peak enemy counts above 550 or capped source damage in runs shorter than 90 minutes. Startup, retry and shared-run loading code moves between chunks without changing those rules. Other balance values, English content descriptions, difficulty settings and wiki icons are unchanged.

Japanese labels now use Japanese fonts installed on the device, with adjusted vertical alignment to centre text on buttons. Tilt-shift rendering now mixes the original scene back into low-alpha pixels to keep those details sharp. Enemy shots use the post-processing blend mode whenever the scene renders to an offscreen target, including tilt-shift without bloom. Game data, English content descriptions, difficulty settings and wiki icons are unchanged. Simulation functions are reordered and renamed without changing their formulas. The Tater Slots jackpot change belongs to game version 19, despite its position in the in-game changelog.

Sir Strawman's seven sickles now slow and return along their heading; Nightmare's fan launches at 130 instead of 120 and no longer curves inward. Returning bullet speed is ×0.7 on Easy, ×1.05 on Normal, Hard and Nightmare (Story ×1); outward speed is unaffected. More effects use crisp pixel art: boss attacks, warning rings, lasso trails, Grok Bots, visitor stun/landing effects, pickups, pools, buildings and ambient dust. Late-loaded poteto and Alex cutscenes now play on slow connections. Cards refit after language fonts load, multilingual text has more room, and the Moldy Shrine menu is shorter with a corrected extra-boss forecast; curse rewards and spawn rules are unchanged. World generation checks nearby cells first and computes sin/cos together without changing the sampled output. Performance telemetry adds median frame work time. Other content tables, English content descriptions and wiki icons are unchanged.

Tibo's enemy-shot hit circle grows from 2.5 to 4 units in radius and moves 2.72 units down towards his feet. Near-miss and bullet-culling distances use the shifted centre too; homing still aims at his unshifted position. Contact and pickup radii are unchanged. The displayed hit circle follows the new position. Adds fuse sparks and heat flashes to Hot Potato and Spicy Hot Potato, distinct pixel-art arcs for Starch Chain, Gratin Arc, Starch Supercell and Grok Bots, sharper Steam Vent and Pressure Cooker rings, and a new revive burst. The in-game changelog adds the hit-circle change and a note about earlier boss/enemy art. Other content values, English content descriptions, difficulty settings and wiki icons are unchanged.

Sprite rendering switches to power-of-two texture-sheet heights and sprite-local texture coordinates, with sampling snapped to a 1/8192-texel grid. Outlines, shadows, projectile sprites and ghost dithering use the local coordinates too. Bright interiors of ground effects are darker and their added glow is slightly reduced. The debug sheetrows URL option now accepts only positive powers of two. The in-game changelog adds a note about notices, such as a dog joining the pack, being centred with the controls hint. Simulation logic, content values, English content descriptions, difficulty settings and wiki icons are unchanged.

The in-game changelog moves seven existing notes from its next section into release ec984b0, dated 2026-11-03: world effects, Sir Strawman's returning sickles, slow-connection Story reveals, font-loading card refits, Chinese/Japanese/Korean text fit, Moldy Shrine menu fit, and Indic/Thai card marks. These are older notes being grouped, not new gameplay changes in this build. Game data, English content descriptions, difficulty settings, simulation and rendering logic, and wiki icons are unchanged.

New game versions can load automatically on the idle Reset screen and before starting another non-Story run from the end screen, preserving the selected difficulty for up to 60 s. A session-storage guard prevents repeated automatic reloads into the same offered build; shared-run parameters are cleared on reload. Update checks also run on the stats screen and use /version.json. Boss death blasts now use two pixel-scaled sprite tiers, sparkles and a separate ground ring; small effect strokes remain visible when downscaled. Rendering caches unchanged overlapping-pool outlines and terrain sample indices, preserves the sharp image when blur is zero, and reports more specific graphics-fallback causes and browser/device categories. The changelog adds the automatic-update note, groups four older notes under earlier releases, and adjusts its narrow layout. Combat data, English content descriptions, difficulty settings, simulation logic and wiki icons are unchanged.

HUD safe-space measurements now subtract sliding banners' CSS translations, including translated ancestors, so layout uses their resting positions instead of their animated positions. This applies to both fresh and cached measurements. The renderer adds an optional half-rate sun-shadow update path, but it defaults off and this build has no caller enabling it; normal shadow updates are unchanged. Shared-run encoding only renames local variables; analytics and the end screen record the new game commit. Combat logic, content values, English content descriptions, difficulty settings and wiki icons are unchanged.

Ordinary pest spawns allow at most two shooters before 3:00 and four before 6:00, then return to the cap of 30. Great Wireworm fires one wider five-shot fan instead of two bursts; its click-beetle shots slow, aim once at Tibo after 0.9 s and accelerate, with earlier retargeting at 0.72 s and a faster finish on Nightmare. Moldy Shrine gold becomes round((45 + 20 × minutes + 2 × minutes²) × gold gain), up from 45 + 9 × minutes before gold gain. Unused Spud Whetstones vanish when weapon slots are full, no eligible weapon can level and no union is currently available; newly generated chunks omit them until that condition clears. Dogs stop pointing at vanished whetstones. Adds Game updated changelog notices after update reloads, a pausing HUD changelog button for relaunched runs, and collapsible older changelog dates. Browsers without WebGL 2 get an explanatory screen with a copyable link instead of the low-detail game. Story reading time excludes pauses and overlays, and reduced-motion lesson panels refit around the cards. Overlapping pools of the same kind share outlines; shot-path previews use thin rose arrows (still hidden on Nightmare). Adds crisp weapon/item effects, dog dash and scent trails, pickup trails/sparkles and revised landing/frost rings. Analytics adds average enemy counts; clipboard, browser detection and card helpers move between chunks. Other content values, English content descriptions, difficulty multipliers and wiki icons are unchanged.

Dog abilities gain ground marks and sparkles: bite impact rings, herd dust rings, bark echoes, fetch stars, dig holes and rescue dust puffs. Herd gusts glow more brightly, add glints and spread more dust; gusts and dust fade behind Tibo to keep him visible. These effects respect reduced-motion, flashes and effects-opacity settings. Simulation logic, content values, English content descriptions, difficulty settings and wiki icons are unchanged.

Item bags and healing snacks get new sprites, coloured glow halos and sparkles. Item bags hop while idle and shake as they charge; snacks pulse. Opening a bag throws confetti, while collecting a snack scatters leaves; both add brief sparkles and a fading halo. Reduced motion uses still poses, and disabling flashes dims burst light and skips the brightest bag-flare frames. The sprite atlas is repacked; other sprite frames and wiki icons are unchanged. Simulation logic, content values, English content descriptions and difficulty settings are unchanged.

Railgun beams now use direction-matched pixel tiles instead of rotated strips, with a bright pulse travelling along the beam; reduced motion skips the pulse. The main renderer compensates for perspective, and the debug renderer snaps the tiles to its pixel grid. Beam scorch marks glow slightly brighter. The sprite atlas is repacked; only the railgun core frames change, and wiki icons are unchanged. The in-game changelog groups eleven existing notes under the older game commit 445c881 rather than treating them as new changes. Simulation logic, content values, English content descriptions and difficulty settings are unchanged.

Interrupted 3D scene downloads now pause play and retry with delays growing from 1 to 8 s; failed early sprite-page downloads can retry too. After a graphics reset, the renderer waits up to 5 s for restoration, then tries a fresh context before falling back. A scene-construction failure retries 3D once on Low at half resolution without adaptive quality; a second construction failure still uses the 2D fallback. Active intro/landing cutscenes end as skipped if the renderer stops being ready. Chest evolution halos use layered gold ground rings with eight rotating dashes instead of three size-specific sprite animations; reduced motion keeps the ring still. The late atlas drops those three clips and repacks the remaining unchanged frames. Adds a translated graphics-recovery changelog note. Combat simulation, existing content/config values, English content descriptions, difficulty settings and wiki icons are unchanged.

Elite pests now break apart in pixel-art death animations with detached gold-rim fragments, in both the main and debug renderers. The main renderer loads separate elite-death and glint sheets through the effects worker, with a main-thread fallback; missing art keeps the ordinary death animation. Fryer King and Late Blight puddles have redrawn, slower surfaces and new boiling bubbles; reduced motion holds the surface and bubble poses still. Root Tunnel gains a closing exit hole and animated clods that bounce and fall back in, with simpler reduced-motion poses; Tibo's outline is hidden while sinking. Shared effects helpers move into separate or consuming chunks, and effect sprites gain horizontal-flip support. Adds a translated elite-death changelog note. Combat simulation is byte-identical after asset-name changes; registry values, extracted gameplay settings, English content descriptions, difficulty settings and wiki icons are unchanged.
